[[Category:Probability distribution]]
[[File:Normal-distribution-p-df.svg|thumbnail|The '''probability density function''' of the normal distribution with different '''parameters''']]
The '''normal distribution''', denoted by $\mathcal{N}(\overline x,\sigma^2)$ is a [[probability distribution]] over $\mathbb{R}$ with the probability density function

$$
\forall x \in \mathbb{R}: f_X(x)=\frac{1}{\sigma\sqrt{2\pi}}
\exp\left(-\frac{(x-\overline x)^2}{2\sigma^2}\right),
$$

where $\overline x, \sigma \in \mathbb{R}$ are the two parameters of the distribution, corresponding to the '''mean''' and the '''standard deviation''' of the real [[random variable]] respectively.

$\mathcal{N}(0,1)$ is known as the '''standard normal distribution'''.

== Properties ==

=== Symmetry over $x=\overline x$ ===

$$
\forall x \in \mathbb{R}: f_X(x)=f_X(2\overline x-x)
$$
